For an entire week, the Holnareem, except for their leader, huddled inside the vault they had dug out of the mountain as the fleshwinds howled. Some of them wept bitterly, believing Koniguldon to be dead. Jamus was particularly grieved, although he tried to hide his feelings.

Then the winds died, but still Koniguldon didn't come.

Jamus instructed the Holnareem to remain in their shelter, suspecting a diabolical trick of some kind. He alone came out onto the mountain. His eyes widened as the bright sun burned down on him... a startling change from the gloomy cold he'd grown accustomed to.

Then he spotted the shadow spilling down from a crag high up the mountain. It disappeared as he ran after it.

His metal heart thudded in his chest as he climbed the seemingly endless rocky slope. At last, he reached the crag.

"Follow me no more," came a rasping voice.

"Koniguldon!" Jamus turned around, trying to find the source of the voice. "We thought you were dead."

"I am." The voice grew distant.

Jamus ran further up the mountain, knocking a stray ant-goat out of his way. "Return to us!"

He saw a dark shape looking down on him from far above. "Come no further. Tell the others you found me dead. Tell them..."

The young, athletic Holnareem pulled himself up a ledge, and stood, facing the shadow. "What has happened?"

He gasped as Koniguldon stepped into the light.

His features were twisted. His metal flesh had blackened and cracked, and his limbs were larger, swollen with power.

His face was an abomination so horrible that Jamus couldn't even look at him without being nauseated.

"The fleshwinds?"

Koniguldon nodded. "They have made a freak of me."

"You are still our leader," Jamus said. But he couldn't even look at him. "I'll go tell them."

"No!" Koniguldon seized him. "You are not to tell them."

Jamus screamed, struggling in his master's grip. "Do not touch me."

Instead of releasing him, Koniguldon crushed him in his embrace. "I'll never let you go," he whispered.

Then, as his bones shattered, Jamus finally realized his leader's true feelings for him. For an instant, he wondered what might have been. Then his spirit departed from his broken body.

Koniguldon wept, and let the body of the friend he had destroyed fall over the ledge. He cursed the gods, yet fell to his knees, praying for mercy from whatever forces might exist. But it was a mercy he didn't truly want.

#

When he returned, holding the body of Jamus, he told the first of many lies to his followers. Jamus had perished helping him fight a powerful demon who had taken him prisoner. No, the demon's body was nowhere to be seen. They didn't question him for long... his fierce, deformed appearance cowed them.

For unknown reasons, the two ill Holnareem soon recovered from their maladies. In the coming days, the camp would be abuzz with talk about the new ore they had discovered, which seemed to have mysterious healing properties. The substance had no apparent effect on Koniguldon, who only became even more hideous with time.

In the coming weeks, their leader would spendmore time alone, as he came to regard his followers as being just as ugly as they regarded him. Meanwhile, they continued manufacturing weapons and other items for trade.

They all believed that the most difficult times were still ahead of them... and soon, this would be proven correct.

Jamus and the Holnareem hid in a cave from the fleshwinds, but get worried about the absence of Koniguldon, their leader. When Jamus goes to look for him after the Fleshwinds died, he finds Koniguldon transformed into a more powerful but less aesthetically pleasing form. Koniguldon kills Janus in a fit of passion, and returns to the rest of the Holnarrem with a tale of demons. The Holnarrem recover due to the Ore from Phyra's planet.

"I liked Phyra."

"I don't care, Image. Keep looking."

"But Phyra seemed nice."

"Good for Phyra. Did you find anything yet?" Oblitus was impatient. While letting Phyra talk with the Image meant another favor he could use, it took longer than expected.

"No, your grace. I see nothing as you described."

"Damn. Follow me then." Oblitus started walking toward the spells quarter of the Nusquam. Towers of shelves with endless scrolls populated the section. "Yes, it should have been here, and it's yet another piece of my collection gone. Ipso must have stolen that one too."

"Stolen what, your grace?" The Image asked.

"He's stolen one of my spells. It prevents anyone from seeing the caster by any other means than being in a physical line of sight..." Oblitus stopped and looked off into a shelf of scrolls. "And it's done it again! Stay here, Image!" Oblitus blinks out of the spells quarter into the physical artifacts quarter.

Standing in a sea of waist high pillars, in front of him was an empty one. "The sword... He took my sword like he took my spells and escaped from my prison." Oblitus raises his hand. Whistling through the air, a staff emerges from the distance. He catches it and taps the ground. "From the forgotten Mages of Unb, I use this Staff of Summoning and call you, Ipso inside the Nusquam to my presence."

A pillar of smoke rushes down and scatters along the ground as [Ipso](https://d2t1xqejof9utc.cloudfront.net/screenshots/pics/283cf1d0beb4d802d7ce81c7006841bd/small.jpg) emerges, towering a foot and a half above Oblitus. The sound of its gears echoes throughout the Nusquam, the glow of a crystal in its chest illuminates the surrounding pillars, and its eyes, a circular shutter, narrows. "That's not fair, Oblitus," Ipso remarked. "I knew you had toys, but I didn't know you had something like that."

"Ipso, you automaton bastard. I don't know how you escaped, but you're going back."

"No, Oblitus, this time I'm not" Ipso lifts [the stolen sword](http://www.legendaryblade.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/Fantasy-Samurai-War-Sword.jpg) and points it at Oblitus. "This says you will let me go."

"You don't even know what that is, Ipso." Oblitus answers. *I must buy some more time. It's clear across the Nusquam from here...* "And even if you did, you don't know how to use it."

"Oh, I do, oh warden. This must be the sword!" Ipso raises the sword high and strikes down. Oblitus barely dodges the strike, his cloak tears from the blade. "And that's my confirmation. The God Edge. Unassuming by appearance, but forged by the heart of a dying god. I saw it as you paraded my cage through your damned Nusquam and I knew what it was. You will let me out of this prison, Oblitus, or I will cut my way out!"

Oblitus looked at Ipso in horror. *It's either too far or caught on something. Either way, this must end within the Nusquam. Both Ipso and the God Edge. If either leaves my domain, every god in Gaea will have my head. If Ipso doesn't cut theirs first!*
